equity.level_reason: The analysis stratifies only by region and age, with no social-position framing of the age results; race/ethnicity and health inequities are raised only in the conclusions as background and a recommendation to prioritize equity.

level_alternative.reason: Age-group increases are reported and the conclusions group children with Black persons under 'health inequities', which could be read as social-position framing of age.

ev.q: Children and non-Hispanic Black or African American persons disproportionately experience asthma exacerbations necessitating emergency care****; extreme weather events might worsen these health inequities
Daily asthma-associated ED visits were compared between the mean of June 1–5 and June 7, 2023, stratified by region and age group.

equity.equity_measurement: No race/ethnicity or socioeconomic data were analysed; the authors cite 'limited covariate data', and the equity statement rests on an external CDC data page.

notes: Agree with the structural record: pre/post comparisons within region and age group meet stratified depth, and region-day correlation with PM2.5 is an ecologic time-series reading. Extreme weather is an environmental exposure, not a social determinant.
